job.title: Senior Payroll Officer

If you are a payroll professional who thrives under pressure, enjoys problem-solving and can hit the ground running, we'd love to hear from you.

job.title: Senior Accountant / Business Services Manager
job.description:
About the Opportunity

Chandler Macleod is partnering with a highly regarded professional services firm to recruit an experienced Senior Accountant or Business Services Manager.

This is an excellent opportunity for a technically strong accounting professional who enjoys working directly with clients and wants to expand their experience across taxation, business advisory, client management and strategic planning.

Working alongside senior leadership, you'll support a diverse client base ranging from privately owned businesses to investors and high-net-worth individuals, while gaining exposure to more complex advisory and commercial matters.

Key Responsibilities

In this role, you will be responsible for the management and delivery of accounting, taxation and advisory services for a varied client portfolio.

Your duties will include:

- Preparing and reviewing financial statements and taxation returns
- Managing annual compliance requirements for a range of entity structures
- Overseeing client work from commencement through to completion
- Building and maintaining strong client relationships
- Assisting with taxation planning and strategic business advice
- Supporting business structuring and asset protection initiatives
- Preparing management reports, financial analysis and cash flow forecasts
- Liaising with regulatory bodies and external stakeholders where required
- Ensuring high standards of accuracy, compliance and professional service delivery
- Developing a thorough understanding of clients' commercial objectives and business operations

About You

To be successful, you will possess:

- Previous experience within Business Services and Taxation
- Strong working knowledge of Australian taxation and accounting regulations
- Experience preparing financial statements and tax returns across various entity structures
- The ability to manage competing deadlines and multiple client engagements
- Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills
- Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities
- A proactive and client-focused approach
- The ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with colleagues and leadership teams
- Relevant tertiary qualifications in Accounting, Commerce or a related discipline
- CA or CPA qualification, or significant progress towards completion, will be highly regarded

Technical Requirements

Candidates must demonstrate experience with:

- Xero Accounting Software
- Xero Tax Solutions

Experience with the following platforms will be advantageous:

- Xero Practice Manager
- Active Ledger
- Class Super
- Microsoft 365 Suite

What's on Offer

This position provides an opportunity to:

- Work closely with experienced senior professionals and decision makers
- Manage a diverse and interesting client portfolio
- Develop expertise beyond traditional compliance accounting
- Gain exposure to business advisory and strategic planning projects
- Build experience across tax planning, restructuring and succession matters
- Strengthen client relationship management and commercial advisory skills
- Progress your career within a supportive and professional environment
- Be part of a firm that values long-term development and technical excellence

Apply Now

If you're an experienced public practice accountant looking to take the next step in your career and broaden your exposure across taxation, advisory and client management, we'd love to hear from you.

job.title: Senior Investment Planning Analyst (Housing & Grid Infrastructure)
job.description:
Senior Investment Planning Analyst
Housing & Grid Infrastructure

Drive the planning and investment decisions that support Western Australia's future growth.

Our client is seeking an experienced Senior Investment Planning Analyst to play a key role in shaping major network infrastructure investment programs that support housing development, grid optimisation, and long-term network performance.

This is a highly visible position that combines strategic planning, portfolio management, financial forecasting, and stakeholder engagement. While advertised as a Senior Investment Planning Analyst, the successful candidate will operate as a Senior Grid Portfolio Analyst, responsible for developing investment plans, managing project pipelines, forecasting expenditure, and supporting critical network infrastructure programs.

About the Role
Working across large-scale housing and grid infrastructure portfolios, you will help ensure the right projects are planned, prioritised, funded, and delivered at the right time. You will provide valuable insights that support investment decisions, network capacity planning, and long-term infrastructure strategy.

This role offers the opportunity to work closely with planning, delivery, finance, and portfolio management teams while contributing to major infrastructure initiatives that support growing communities across Western Australia.

Key Responsibilities
Portfolio & Investment Planning
  • Develop and maintain short and long-term investment plans across housing and grid optimisation portfolios.
  • Build and manage multi-year project pipelines aligned with strategic network objectives.
  • Identify project dependencies, approval pathways, critical milestones, and delivery risks.
  • Support annual planning cycles and long-term network investment strategies.
Budgeting & Forecasting
  • Develop and maintain portfolio budgets and expenditure forecasts.
  • Translate capital investment plans into accurate monthly and annual financial forecasts.
  • Maintain rolling expenditure forecasts and analyse variances against budget.
  • Provide recommendations and insights to support investment decision-making.
Housing & Infrastructure Program Planning
  • Monitor infrastructure requirements associated with housing growth initiatives.
  • Analyse network capacity, anticipated housing developments, and energisation timelines.
  • Assess future investment requirements and identify potential capacity constraints.
  • Develop planning scenarios to support prioritisation and risk assessment.
Project Pipeline Management
  • Maintain a forward-looking portfolio of infrastructure projects.
  • Support resource planning, investment prioritisation, and governance processes.
  • Monitor project readiness and ensure key approvals are achieved within required timeframes.
  • Track delivery risks and emerging portfolio challenges.
Stakeholder Engagement & Reporting
  • Partner with cross-functional stakeholders across planning, delivery, finance, and portfolio teams.
  • Produce reports, forecasts, and analysis for senior leaders and decision-makers.
  • Develop tools, dashboards, and reporting processes that improve planning accuracy and visibility.
  • Drive continuous improvement initiatives across forecasting and portfolio management practices.
About You
  • Experience managing investment plans, project portfolios, infrastructure programs, or complex project schedules.
  • Strong financial modelling, budgeting, forecasting, and analytical capabilities.
  • The ability to interpret complex data and translate it into meaningful business insights.
  • Experience balancing multiple priorities, dependencies, resources, and delivery timelines.
  • Excellent stakeholder engagement and relationship-building skills.
  • Strong problem-solving skills with the ability to evaluate risks and provide practical recommendations.
  • Advanced Excel and data analysis capability, with experience using planning and reporting tools.
  • Experience within utilities, infrastructure, energy, transport, resources, or other asset-intensive environments highly regarded.
Why Apply? This is an opportunity to join a high-performing team where your work will directly influence major infrastructure investment decisions. You'll play a critical role in ensuring future housing developments and network infrastructure programs are supported by sound planning, robust forecasting, and effective portfolio management.

If you're an experienced portfolio, planning, or investment professional looking to make a meaningful impact on large-scale infrastructure programs, we would love to hear from you.

Our client is seeking a reliable and experienced MR Truck Driver / Forklift Operator to join the team within the fruit and vegetable packaging industry.

You will be responsible for completing deliveries throughout Adelaide's northern suburbs and surrounding market garden regions while assisting with loading, unloading, and general warehouse duties when required.   • Previous truck driving and forklift operating experience.
  • Experience loading and unloading vehicles safely.
  • Strong time management and organisational skills.
  • Ability to work independently and manage daily delivery schedules.
  • Good customer service and communication skills.
  • Understanding of load restraint and safe manual handling practices.
  • Strong commitment to workplace safety.
 
Working Hours

During the winter season, employees can expect a minimum of approximately 28-30 hours per week.
During the summer peak season, working hours increase significantly, with regular overtime opportunities available. Saturday work may also be required during busy periods.

Our client, a Tier1 mining company is seeking a Project Manager to lead the implementation and rollout of its Environmental Data Management System (EQUIS) across multiple operational sites. This is a business-led project within the Environment function and is not a software development or IT infrastructure role.

We are specifically seeking a Project Manager who has delivered environmental, compliance, monitoring, operational, sustainability, HSE, EHS, environmental reporting or environmental data management projects within mining, resources, industrial, utilities or heavy industry environments.

  • Drive site-by-site deployment and business adoption

Essential Experience

To be considered, you must demonstrate experience delivering projects involving one or more of the following:

  • Environmental monitoring programs

  • Environmental compliance or regulatory reporting

  • Environmental management systems

  • Environmental data management systems (EDMS)

  • HSE / EHS systems

  • Sustainability or compliance systems

  • Site-based operational improvement projects

  • Environmental remediation, groundwater, air quality, emissions, waste or water management projects

You will also bring:

  • Proven project delivery experience within mining, resources, industrial, manufacturing, utilities or heavy industry sectors

  • Strong stakeholder engagement and vendor management capability

  • Experience managing project budgets, reporting and governance requirements

  • Ability to coordinate multidisciplinary teams across multiple locations

Highly Regarded

  • Environmental science, environmental engineering or environmental management background

  • Experience with EQUIS, Envirosys, Intelex, Cority, Enablon, Sphera, SAP EHS or similar platforms

  • Multi-site implementation experience

  • Formal Project Management qualifications

This role is ideally suited to an Environmental Project Manager, Environmental Consultant, Environmental Program Manager, Compliance Project Manager, HSE Project Manager or Operational Project Manager with experience delivering environmental or compliance-related initiatives across complex operational environments.

job.title: Senior Planner - Decarbonisation Delivery & Assets
job.description:
Senior Planner - Decarbonisation Delivery & Assets
Location: Perth CBD
Roster: 5:2
Contract: ASAP Start | Until June 2027

About the Role

We are seeking an experienced Senior Planner to support a major decarbonisation program involving renewable energy infrastructure, electrification initiatives, battery-electric mining fleets, OEM development programs and operational transition activities.
This role will be responsible for developing, maintaining and optimising integrated project schedules across a diverse portfolio of capital projects, ensuring successful delivery from concept and engineering through to commissioning, operational readiness and handover.
Working within a high-performing project services team, you will collaborate closely with project delivery, engineering, procurement, operations, contractors and OEM partners to provide schedule leadership, performance analysis and project controls support.

Key Responsibilities
  • Develop and maintain integrated master schedules and detailed project schedules across multiple decarbonisation projects.
  • Coordinate engineering, procurement, construction, commissioning, fleet readiness and operational transition activities within portfolio schedules.
  • Develop resource, commodity and cost-loaded schedules.
  • Perform critical path analysis, milestone tracking and "what-if" scenario planning.
  • Maintain schedule integrity through logic reviews, schedule health checks and planning best practices.
  • Implement Earned Value Management (EVM) and analyse schedule performance, including CPI and SPI reporting.
  • Review and integrate contractor, supplier and OEM schedules into master project programs.
  • Identify schedule risks, opportunities and emerging trends, providing proactive recommendations to project teams.
  • Prepare weekly and monthly progress, performance and forecasting reports.
  • Participate in schedule reviews, risk workshops, change management processes and capital planning activities.
About You
Essential Experience
  • Minimum 10 years' experience in project planning and scheduling.
  • Proven client-side experience across the full project lifecycle, from concept through to execution and handover.
  • Experience supporting major capital projects within mining, resources, energy, infrastructure or industrial sectors.
  • Strong understanding of project controls, scheduling methodologies and project governance.
  • Demonstrated experience integrating multiple contractor, supplier and operational schedules.
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.
  • Ability to work autonomously and effectively within multidisciplinary teams.
  • Strong commitment to health, safety and environmental standards.
Technical Skills
  • Advanced Primavera P6 experience.
  • Strong Microsoft Office Suite skills.
  • Experience using Power BI or similar reporting and business intelligence tools.
  • Sound understanding of Earned Value Management (EVM) principles and performance reporting.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving capability.
Desirable Qualifications
  • Tertiary qualification in Engineering, Project Management or a related discipline.
  • Project Controls, Planning or Scheduling certification.
  • Experience in mining fleet electrification, OEM programs or decarbonisation initiatives.
What's on Offer
  • ASAP start
  • Long-term contract through to June 2027
  • Perth CBD location
  • Monday to Friday (5:2 roster)
  • Opportunity to contribute to a significant decarbonisation and electrification program
  • Collaborative and high-performing project environment
  • Exposure to large-scale infrastructure, energy and mobile asset projects
If you are an experienced Planner with strong Primavera P6 expertise and a passion for delivering complex projects, we would like to hear from you.

An exciting opportunity exists for an experienced and commercially focused Senior Finance Manager to join a leading global heavy equipment organisation. Reporting directly to the General Manager, this role will take ownership of the company's equipment financing operations across Australia, driving finance penetration, supporting sales growth, managing credit risk, and building strong customer and dealer relationships.

This is a highly visible position that combines, portfolio management, credit oversight, and strategic stakeholder engagement. The successful candidate will work closely with local teams and international headquarters to deliver financing solutions that support business growth and customer success.

International travel flexibility is required, with periodic travel to regional offices, dealer partners, and company headquarters across the Asia Pacific region.

Essential Requirements

  • HV switching (or exposure to HV environments)

  • SAP / maintenance management experience

Reporting to the Project Manager, you will work within a small, collaborative team and apply your expertise across logistics management, inventory systems, technical documentation, codification, stakeholder engagement, and sustainment planning.

  • Strong understanding of Defence logistics policies, processes and frameworks.
  • Experience developing and managing logistics support documentation and artefacts.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.

  • Ability to obtain and maintain a Baseline Security Clearance.

This role offers an excellent opportunity to gain experience within the resources sector while developing a broad range of administrative and operational support skills.

Key Responsibilities

  • Create and format PowerPoint presentations, reports, and business documents.
  • Manage calendars and schedule meetings for management and site personnel.
  • Coordinate meeting invitations and meeting room bookings.
  • Raise and track purchase orders and assist with invoice processing.

  • Maintain accurate electronic filing systems and records.
  • Prepare meeting agendas, minutes, and action logs.
  • Order stationery, PPE, kitchen supplies, and other site consumables.
  • Liaise with suppliers, contractors, and internal stakeholders.
  • Support document control and compliance administration activities.
  • Monitor office supplies and maintain shared office and kitchen areas.
  • Provide general administrative support to site and corporate teams.
Skills & Experience

Essential

  • Strong Microsoft Office skills, particularly PowerPoint, Word, Outlook, and Excel.
  • Excellent organisational and time management skills.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • High level of attention to detail.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities in a busy environment.
  • Professional, positive, and customer-focused approach.
  • Current Driver's Licence.
Desirable

  • Previous administration, reception, or office support experience.
  • Exposure to mining, construction, engineering, or industrial environments.
  • Experience with purchase orders and invoice processing.
  • Experience using Microsoft Teams and SharePoint.
  • Understanding of site-based or FIFO/DIDO operations.
Personal Attributes

  • Positive and enthusiastic attitude.
  • Reliable and dependable.
  • Strong team player.
  • Willingness to assist with a broad range of administrative duties.
  • Adaptable and capable of working autonomously.
  • Eager to learn and develop within the mining industry.
What We Offer

  • Entry into the mining and resources sector.
  • Supportive and collaborative team environment.
  • Career development opportunities.
  • Exposure to a wide range of business and operational functions.
  • Ongoing training and mentoring.
This role would suit a recent school leaver, TAFE graduate, university graduate, or someone with 1-2 years of administration experience looking to build a long-term career within the mining and resources industry.

job.title: Construction Estimator
job.description:
Estimator | Shepparton VIC

Chandler Macleod are recruiting for an Estimator on behalf of a well-established and growing construction business based in Shepparton.

This is an exciting opportunity to join a respected regional organisation that places a strong emphasis on quality, customer experience, collaboration and continuous improvement.

Whether you're an experienced Estimator, a Draftsperson looking to move into estimating, or a construction professional with strong technical and systems aptitude, this role offers the opportunity to make a genuine impact within a growing business.

The Opportunity As Estimator, you will take ownership of project estimating, pricing and purchasing functions, ensuring residential construction projects are accurately costed and commercially managed from pre-construction through to handover.

You will work closely with internal stakeholders, trades and suppliers while contributing to process improvements, systems optimisation and business growth initiatives.

Key Responsibilities
  • Prepare detailed quantity take-offs and cost estimates from architectural plans and documentation.
  • Maintain and improve estimating systems, cost databases and price books.
  • Generate and manage purchase orders with approved suppliers and subcontractors.
  • Review project budgets and identify opportunities to improve cost efficiency and profitability.
  • Support sales and operational teams with accurate pricing information and cost advice.
  • Identify potential risks, budget overruns and delivery issues before they become project impacts.
  • Build strong relationships with suppliers, subcontractors and internal stakeholders.
  • Visit project sites as required to assess variations, resolve issues and support project outcomes.
About You We are interested in candidates from a range of construction-related backgrounds, including:

  • Residential or Commercial Estimating
  • Drafting and plan interpretation
  • Construction, carpentry or building trades transitioning off the tools
  • Building materials, supplier or manufacturing environments
  • Technical, engineering or project support roles with strong systems capability
To be successful, you'll demonstrate:

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
  • High attention to detail and accuracy
  • Excellent computer literacy, including Excel and estimating software
  • A continuous improvement mindset
  • The ability to build trusted relationships with suppliers, trades and colleagues
  • Strong communication skills and a collaborative approach
  • A genuine desire to establish a long-term career within a regional business
What's On Offer
  • Competitive salary package from $100,000+ plus superannuation, negotiable based on experience
  • Full-time permanent position
  • Monday to Friday, 8:30am to 5:00pm
  • Supportive leadership and direct mentoring from experienced industry professionals
  • Opportunity to influence systems, processes and business improvement initiatives
  • Modern office environment and strong team culture
  • Long-term career growth within an expanding regional organisation
Requirements
  • Australian Citizenship or Permanent Residency
  • Current driver's licence and reliable transport
  • Ability to work from the Shepparton region and maintain a sustainable daily commute
  • Experience within construction, estimating, drafting, building, procurement or a related discipline
Apply Now If you're looking for a rewarding opportunity to combine your construction knowledge, technical capability and commercial mindset with a growing regional employer, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply now through Chandler Macleod with your current resume and a brief cover letter outlining your experience and interest in the role.

job.title: Project Assurance Officer
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is seeking an experienced Project Assurance Officer to join a Federal Government client on a contract opportunity. This role is ideal for a governance, assurance, risk, or project management professional who enjoys analysing project performance, identifying opportunities for improvement, and supporting successful project delivery outcomes.

Working under limited direction, you will play an important role in supporting project governance and assurance activities across a diverse project portfolio, ensuring projects are delivered in alignment with established frameworks, standards, and organisational objectives.



About the Role As a Project Assurance Officer, you will contribute to the oversight and continuous improvement of project delivery by conducting assurance activities, reviewing project documentation and reporting, identifying emerging risks and issues, and providing evidence-based advice to project teams and senior stakeholders.
You will work closely with project managers, governance bodies, and subject matter experts to strengthen project management practices and support informed decision-making across a complex portfolio of work.

Key Responsibilities
  • Conduct project assurance activities in line with established frameworks, processes, and standards.
  • Review project documentation, governance arrangements, schedules, budgets, risks, issues, benefits, and reporting artefacts.
  • Analyse project performance information and assurance evidence to identify trends, risks, gaps, and opportunities for improvement.
  • Prepare high-quality reports, briefs, governance papers, dashboards, and recommendations for senior stakeholders and decision-makers.
  • Support executive oversight through the provision of clear, evidence-based advice.
  • Build productive relationships with project managers, senior responsible officers, and key stakeholders.
  • Contribute to the improvement of project governance, assurance frameworks, templates, guidance material, and reporting processes.
  • Support the coordination of governance forums, including agenda preparation, action tracking, decision registers, and follow-up activities.
  • Escalate emerging risks, issues, and areas of non-compliance where required.
  • Promote consistent project management practices and support capability uplift initiatives across project teams.
About You To be successful in this role, you will demonstrate:
  • Experience in project management, governance, assurance, risk management, reporting, evaluation, or a related discipline.
  • Sound understanding of project lifecycle management, including planning, governance, risk and issue management, scheduling, benefits management, reporting, and assurance practices.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to interpret information from multiple sources and identify key risks and insights.
  • Excellent written communication skills, with experience preparing briefs, reports, committee papers, dashboards, and executive-level advice.
  • Strong verbal communication and stakeholder engagement skills.
  • Ability to build and maintain productive working relationships across diverse stakeholder groups.
  • Sound judgement, initiative, and the ability to work independently while managing competing priorities.
  • High attention to detail and commitment to delivering accurate, quality outcomes within deadlines.
  • A proactive approach to continuous improvement and enhancing governance and assurance practices.
Highly Desirable
  • Experience supporting governance committees, project assurance reviews, portfolio reporting, or enterprise project management functions.
  • Experience contributing to project capability uplift initiatives, process improvement activities, or assurance frameworks.
  • Qualifications or training in project management, governance, assurance, risk management, business analysis, evaluation, or related fields.
Security Requirements
  • Must hold, or have the ability to obtain and maintain, a Baseline Security Clearance.

If you have a passion for project governance, assurance, and continuous improvement, we encourage you to apply today.

job.title: Content Designer
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is seeking a talented APS5 Content Designer to join a Federal Government client on an initial 12-month contract, with the possibility of a further 12-month extension.
This is an excellent opportunity for a digital content professional who is passionate about creating accessible, user-centred online experiences. You'll be responsible for developing and maintaining high-quality website content that helps users find information, understand services, and complete tasks with confidence.
Location
  • Canberra ACT
  • Sydney NSW
  • Brisbane QLD
Contract Details
  • Initial 12-month contract
  • Potential 12-month extension
  • Hybrid working arrangements
  • 37.5 hours per week
  • Estimated start: October 2026
About the Role As a Content Designer, you will support the creation, maintenance, and continuous improvement of digital content across web and online communication channels. Working within a collaborative digital environment, you will partner with subject matter experts, policy teams, service owners, and technical specialists to design content that is clear, accessible, and focused on user needs.
You will play a key role in transforming complex information into simple, engaging content while ensuring compliance with Australian Government digital standards and accessibility requirements.
Key Responsibilities
  • Create, edit and publish digital content using content management systems, including GovCMS.
  • Develop clear, concise and user-focused content written in plain English.
  • Conduct content reviews, audits and remediation activities to improve quality and consistency.
  • Apply content design principles and best practice digital communication standards.
  • Work closely with stakeholders to gather information and convert complex material into accessible content.
  • Support website governance activities, publishing workflows and content lifecycle management.
  • Contribute to user research, usability testing and content improvement initiatives.
  • Assist in developing information architecture and content structures that improve the user experience.
  • Ensure content aligns with accessibility requirements and government digital standards.
About You To be successful in this role, you will demonstrate:
  • Experience writing and editing clear, concise, audience-focused content in plain English.
  • Understanding of content design, digital communications and user-centred design principles.
  • Experience working with content management systems, preferably Drupal or GovCMS.
  • Knowledge of the Australian Government Digital Service Standard, Style Manual and WCAG accessibility requirements.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and relationship management skills.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.
  • A collaborative approach and the ability to work effectively within multidisciplinary teams.
Highly Desirable
  • Qualifications in Communications, Journalism, Professional Writing, Digital Media, Marketing, Public Relations or a related discipline.
  • Experience using web analytics tools such as Google Analytics.
  • Understanding of SEO principles and writing content for digital channels.
  • Experience working in Agile or multidisciplinary digital delivery teams.
Security Requirements
  • Must be able to obtain and maintain a Baseline Security Clearance.

How to Apply As part of the application process, candidates will be required to provide a one-page pitch addressing the selection criteria.

Apply now to be considered for this exciting APS5 Content Designer opportunity with Chandler Macleod's Federal Government client. - Aparna Garg aparna.garg@chandlermacleod.com

job.title: Track Protection Officer
job.description:
Track Protection Officer | Rio Tinto Rail Network | FIFO 12/9 roster with a mix of days and nights. 
We are seeking safety-focused and motivated Track Protection Officers (TPOs) to support ballast cleaning operations across a heavy haul rail maintenance environment. This is an excellent opportunity to work within a high-performing team, contribute to critical maintenance activities, and ensure the highest standards of rail safety and compliance are maintained.

What You'll Do:
  • Prepare, verify and implement Track Protection Plans and work-on-track authority requirements.
  • Confirm worksite limits, access points, safe places, adjacent line risks and protection requirements prior to commencing work.
  • Establish, maintain and remove field protection controls in accordance with approved safeworking requirements.
  • Conduct comprehensive pre-start and safeworking briefings, including sign-on processes, worksite limits, hazards and emergency arrangements.
  • Coordinate closely with supervisors, PPOs, Train Control, maintainers, contractors, operators and ballast cleaning crews to ensure safe work execution.
  • Monitor changing worksite conditions, rail traffic exposure, machine movements, fatigue risks, weather impacts and scope changes.
  • Exercise the authority to stop work and escalate concerns immediately where protection, communication, authority or behaviours are unsafe or non-compliant.
  • Complete all required documentation, handovers, authority cancellations and close-out records accurately and within required timeframes.
  • Ensure all personnel remain protected through effective planning, communication and compliance with rail safeworking standards.
Required Skills:
  • Strong understanding of rail safeworking principles, track protection requirements and operational risk controls.
  • Excellent safety-critical communication skills with the ability to liaise effectively with Train Control, supervisors, contractors and operational personnel.
  • Ability to work independently, remain focused under pressure and make sound safety-based decisions.
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to procedural compliance and critical risk management.
  • Ability to monitor dynamic work environments and proactively respond to changing operational conditions.
Desirable Skills:
  • Current Track Protection Officer competency for the relevant rail network.
  • Experience working within heavy haul rail, maintenance shutdowns, possessions or major maintenance campaigns.
  • Strong understanding of work authorities, protection methods, field protection arrangements and multi-workgroup environments.
  • Experience supporting rail maintenance activities such as ballast cleaning, tamping, rail grinding, renewals or track machine operations.
  • Ability to interpret track schematics, obstruction plans, work packs and maintenance scopes.
  • Exposure to Pilbara rail operations, work management systems, incident reporting and safety management processes.
Preferred Experience:
  • Previous experience as a Track Protection Officer, Protection Officer or safeworking professional within rail maintenance, possession or heavy haul rail environments.
  • Current rail safety worker medical clearance (preferably Category 1 where required) and relevant rail corridor access or rail safety awareness qualifications.
  • Proven ability to coordinate and manage rail protection requirements in high-risk operational environments.
  • Demonstrated experience supporting maintenance crews, contractors, rail vehicles and mobile plant within live rail corridors.
  • Strong knowledge of safeworking systems, permits, protection authorities and rail operating rules.
Other Requirements:
  • Ability to meet Rio Tinto onboarding, site access, verification of competency (VOC) and fitness-for-work requirements.
  • Valid Australian C-Class Driver's Licence.
  • Willingness and ability to travel to and mobilise within remote rail worksites as required.
  • Able to work a 12/9 roster with a mix of days and nights aswell as various swing durations.
  • Strong safety mindset with the confidence to challenge unsafe conditions, stop work when required and escalate risks appropriately.
  • Commitment to fostering a positive safety culture through leadership, coaching and professional conduct.
If you are a safety-driven rail professional with experience in track protection, possessions or rail maintenance operations, we want to hear from you. This is your opportunity to contribute to critical ballast cleaning and rail maintenance activities while working within a leading heavy haul rail environment.
Apply now and become a key contributor to safe, compliant and successful rail operations across the Pilbara rail network.


At Chandler Macleod, we are committed to fostering a diverse workforce where everyone is welcome. We encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, women, neurodiverse, people living with a disability and the LGBTIQA+ community.

You can read more about our commitment to diversity and inclusion at https://www.chandlermacleod.com/diversity-and-inclusion.

Dispatch EOI
Mon-Fri + Overtime|$32.82 + penalty

job.title: Project Assurance Officer

This role is ideal for a governance, assurance, risk, or project management professional who enjoys analysing project performance, identifying opportunities for improvement, and supporting successful project delivery outcomes.

About the Role As a Project Assurance Officer, you will contribute to the oversight and continuous improvement of project delivery by conducting assurance activities, reviewing project documentation and reporting, identifying emerging risks and issues, and providing evidence-based advice to project teams and senior stakeholders.
You will work closely with project managers, governance bodies, and subject matter experts to strengthen project management practices and support informed decision-making across a complex portfolio of work.

Key Responsibilities
  • Conduct project assurance activities in line with established frameworks, processes, and standards.
  • Review project documentation, governance arrangements, schedules, budgets, risks, issues, benefits, and reporting artefacts.
  • Analyse project performance information and assurance evidence to identify trends, risks, gaps, and opportunities for improvement.
  • Prepare high-quality reports, briefs, governance papers, dashboards, and recommendations for senior stakeholders and decision-makers.
  • Support executive oversight through the provision of clear, evidence-based advice.
  • Build productive relationships with project managers, senior responsible officers, and key stakeholders.
  • Contribute to the improvement of project governance, assurance frameworks, templates, guidance material, and reporting processes.
  • Support the coordination of governance forums, including agenda preparation, action tracking, decision registers, and follow-up activities.
  • Escalate emerging risks, issues, and areas of non-compliance where required.
  • Promote consistent project management practices and support capability uplift initiatives across project teams.
About You To be successful in this role, you will demonstrate:
  • Experience in project management, governance, assurance, risk management, reporting, evaluation, or a related discipline.
  • Sound understanding of project lifecycle management, including planning, governance, risk and issue management, scheduling, benefits management, reporting, and assurance practices.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to interpret information from multiple sources and identify key risks and insights.
  • Excellent written communication skills, with experience preparing briefs, reports, committee papers, dashboards, and executive-level advice.
  • Strong verbal communication and stakeholder engagement skills.
  • Ability to build and maintain productive working relationships across diverse stakeholder groups.
  • Sound judgement, initiative, and the ability to work independently while managing competing priorities.
  • High attention to detail and commitment to delivering accurate, quality outcomes within deadlines.
  • A proactive approach to continuous improvement and enhancing governance and assurance practices.
Highly Desirable
  • Experience supporting governance committees, project assurance reviews, portfolio reporting, or enterprise project management functions.
  • Experience contributing to project capability uplift initiatives, process improvement activities, or assurance frameworks.
  • Qualifications or training in project management, governance, assurance, risk management, business analysis, evaluation, or related fields.
Security Requirements
  • Must hold, or have the ability to obtain and maintain, a Baseline Security Clearance.

If you have a passion for project governance, assurance, and continuous improvement, we encourage you to apply today.

job.description:
Chandler Macleod is recruiting on behalf of our Federal Government client for an experienced Audit and Assurance Officer to join their Governance team in Canberra. This is a 12 month, full time labour hire contract.
This is an excellent opportunity for a governance, audit, risk, or assurance professional to contribute to the delivery of effective governance frameworks, organisational resilience, risk management, and continuous improvement initiatives within a high-profile Commonwealth agency.

About the Role
The Audit and Assurance Officer plays a key role in supporting the agency's governance, audit, assurance, risk management, and business continuity functions.
Working closely with internal stakeholders, service providers, and governance committees, you will coordinate internal audits, monitor audit recommendations, support risk and assurance activities, and contribute to the ongoing improvement of governance and risk frameworks. You will also assist in strengthening organisational resilience through the management and coordination of business continuity planning and testing activities.

Key Responsibilities
As the Audit and Assurance Officer, you will:
  • Manage relationships and contracts with internal audit service providers, ensuring accountability and delivery against agreed milestones.
  • Coordinate the delivery of internal audits in accordance with the Annual Internal Audit Plan.
  • Liaise with stakeholders, facilitate information gathering, track audit progress, and support audit activities from commencement through to completion.
  • Maintain audit recommendation registers and monitor the implementation, reporting, escalation, and closure of management actions.
  • Prepare high-quality reports, briefings, and committee papers relating to audit, assurance, risk management, and business continuity matters.
  • Contribute to the continuous improvement of governance, audit, assurance, and risk management frameworks.
  • Coordinate quality assurance activities and support annual assessments of internal audit service effectiveness.
  • Support the effective operation of governance and oversight committees, including member onboarding and administrative coordination.
  • Coordinate external reviews, assurance activities, compliance assessments, and risk workshops.
  • Manage and maintain business continuity arrangements, including planning, testing exercises, resilience initiatives, and monitoring improvement actions.
  • Provide specialist advice on governance, audit, assurance, risk, and business continuity matters across the organisation.
About You
To be successful in this role, you will have demonstrated experience in governance, audit, assurance, risk management, compliance, or related fields within a government or highly regulated environment.

You will bring:
Audit, Risk & Assurance Expertise
  • Experience coordinating internal audit programs and assurance activities.
  • Strong understanding of governance, risk management, and control frameworks.
  • Knowledge of Australian Government audit, risk, and assurance principles.
  • Experience managing audit findings, recommendations, and reporting processes.
  • Understanding of business continuity planning and organisational resilience practices.
Strategic Thinking & Analysis
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to interpret complex information, identify emerging trends, and recommend practical improvements.
  • Experience contributing to strategic planning and assurance priorities.
  • Understanding of performance metrics, data analysis, and reporting.
Communication & Stakeholder Engagement
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Experience preparing executive-level reports, briefing papers, and committee documentation.
  • Ability to influence, negotiate, and build credibility with senior stakeholders.
  • Strong relationship management and contract management capabilities.
Personal Effectiveness
  • Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively across geographically dispersed teams.
  • Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage competing priorities and meet deadlines.
  • High attention to detail and commitment to quality outcomes.
  • Sound judgement and the ability to provide trusted advice on complex governance and assurance matters.
 
Apply Now

job.title: Solution Architect - AI
job.description:
We are seeking an experienced AI Solution Architect with deep expertise in Data, AI/ML, Microsoft AI Foundry and Databricks to join our client AGL and lead the design and delivery of scalable, secure, and production-ready AI solutions. This is a six-month contract role with a potential to extend for longer based in Melbourne Docklands offices in a hybrid working environment.

This is a hands-on architecture role where you will work closely with engineering teams, platform architects, data scientists, and business stakeholders to translate complex business requirements into practical, executable solution designs. You will play a critical role in shaping end-to-end AI and machine learning solutions, guiding implementation decisions, and supporting delivery teams through build, integration, testing, and deployment.

This opportunity is ideal for someone who enjoys balancing strategic architecture with hands-on technical leadership and is passionate about applying emerging AI technologies to solve real business challenges.

Key Responsibilities
  • Lead the architecture and delivery of end-to-end AI/ML solutions, from data ingestion and transformation through to deployment, monitoring, and optimisation.
  • Produce detailed, engineering-ready solution designs covering architecture, integrations, APIs, data flows, security, deployment models, and operational support.
  • Design and implement AI solutions using Microsoft AI Foundry, Azure AI services, Databricks, and modern data platforms.
  • Architect agentic AI, RAG, LLM, and generative AI solutions, including prompt engineering and multi-agent frameworks.
  • Act as the technical SME for the Azure AI ecosystem, including Azure AI Foundry, Azure OpenAI, Azure ML, Microsoft Fabric, and Databricks.
  • Evaluate, integrate, and govern emerging AI models and technologies, balancing performance, security, scalability, and cost.
  • Design AI gateway patterns, security controls, model routing, content safety mechanisms, and responsible AI guardrails.
  • Partner with architects, engineers, data scientists, delivery teams, and business stakeholders to define requirements and drive successful outcomes.
  • Ensure solutions align with enterprise architecture standards, governance frameworks, security requirements, and best practices.
  • Provide technical leadership throughout delivery, supporting implementation planning, risk assessment, and adoption of practical engineering approaches.


About You
You are a technically strong Architect with a proven track record delivering enterprise-scale Data and AI solutions. You have the ability to move seamlessly between strategy, architecture, and hands-on implementation while influencing technical and business stakeholders alike.
You will have
  • Proven experience in Solution Architecture, Data Architecture, or a similar technical leadership role.
  • Proven experience delivering AI/ML solutions in enterprise environments.
  • Proven hands-on experience designing and deploying AI/ML solutions within the Microsoft Azure and Databricks ecosystem.
  • Strong expertise across:
    • Azure AI Foundry
    • Azure OpenAI Service
    • Azure ML
    • Microsoft Fabric
    • Databricks
    • Delta Lake
    • Unity Catalog
    • MLflow
Technical Expertise
  • Deep understanding of NLP, transformer architectures, Large Language Models (LLMs), and generative AI solutions.
  • Strong experience with AI/ML frameworks and libraries such as TensorFlow, PyTorch, Hugging Face, SpaCy, and NLTK.
  • Hands-on experience with prompt engineering, RAG implementations, agentic AI concepts, autonomous agents, and Model Context Protocol (MCP).
  • Strong data architecture background including data modelling, data warehousing, ETL/ELT, integration patterns, and modern data platforms.
  • Experience building detailed, engineering-ready solution designs covering security, APIs, integrations, deployment, and operational support requirements.
Soft Skills
  • Exceptional communication and stakeholder management skills.
  • Ability to influence technical and non-technical audiences, including executive stakeholders.
  • Strong problem-solving skills with a pragmatic, delivery-focused mindset.

Apply now if you have a strong background in AI solution architecture and are passionate about delivering enterprise-scale AI capabilities that create real business value.

job.description:

Our client is a large federal government agency focused on providing high-quality mental health assessment and clinical counselling services. They take pride on meeting client needs through a combination of proven clinical practices and new and emerging evidence-based approaches. Reporting to the Assistant Director, you will work with a professional team who are all dedicated to making a different in the lives of their clients.

This position offers a rewarding chance to impact lives positively while expanding your professional experience in a supportive, mission-driven setting.
 
  • Support regional teams by reviewing and allocating clients for counselling services, ensuring they are suitable for both initial and ongoing support in line with service guidelines.

  • Follow all relevant laws, ethical standards, and policies related to client care.
  • Meet regularly with your manager and other clinicians to discuss client progress and care plans.
  • Work with clients’ families and other treatment providers to make sure care is well-coordinated.
  • Contribute to a safe, supportive, and professional work environment that aligns with organisational values and goals.


About you:

  • You will have extensive case management experience

job.title: Group Finance Manager
job.description:
Group Finance Manager, Multi-Entity Private Group
Campbelfield 

Our client is a privately owned, founder-led group of businesses with a combined annual turnover exceeding $30 million. The Group spans six operating entities across bin hire and property development, waste services, legal services, agriculture and wellness, all wholly owned by a single Director who moves fast and runs multiple projects at once.

This is not a conventional Group Finance Manager role. It's a genuine seat at the table with a founder who has built serious value across his businesses but knows his financial oversight hasn't kept pace with growth. Fund flows between entities haven't always been formally documented, and there's currently no single consolidated view of the Group's debt, cash or net asset position.

You'll be the first person to sit across the entire Group with a clear mandate: bring order, structure and visibility to the Director's complete financial position, business and personal.

Responsibilities
  • Owning the Group's consolidated financial position at all times, with the Director able to get an accurate answer to any financial question within the hour
  • Managing everything from personal expenses through to major capital requirements for property acquisitions and construction
  • Rolling cash flow forecasts and a weekly cash and debt summary for the Director
  • Overseeing the bookkeeping team and liaising with the external tax agent on compliance
  • Building and enforcing clear financial controls, including a formal intercompany transfer process
  • Supporting evaluation of new property acquisitions, including development feasibility modelling
  • Managing banking relationships and lender communication across a large number of accounts
What We're Looking For:
  • 7+ years in a senior finance role, ideally across multiple entities or a group structure
  • Hands-on experience with property development finance: construction loans, feasibility, project cost control
  • Comfortable working directly with a founder where priorities shift fast; you're a stabilising force, not an extra variable
  • Advanced Xero skills across multiple entities, without needing support
  • Experience managing or directing bookkeepers and junior finance staff
  • CPA or CA preferred, though exceptional experience will be considered in place of it
  • Absolute discretion; you'll have full visibility of the Director's personal and business financial position
Why This Role:

 At 30 days, you'll have delivered a complete financial map of the Group. At 6 months, clear controls are in place and the Director gets a weekly summary he can rely on. At 12 months, you're his most trusted operational partner, contributing directly to decisions on acquisitions, cash deployment and growth.

This is a genuinely broad, high-trust mandate for someone who wants ownership, not just oversight.

To apply, submit your CV along with a short cover note on why this particular role, its pace, complexity and scope, appeals to you.

This contract offers the opportunity to contribute to a landmark transport infrastructure project within one of South East Queensland’s fastest-growing regions.

  • Ability to provide high-level written and verbal advice to a range of technical and senior stakeholders. 
  • Experience working across multidisciplinary project teams in government, consulting or infrastructure environments.
  • Degree qualifications in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Environmental Management, Natural Resource Management or a related discipline.

job.title: Fitter
job.description:
Fitter

Chandler Macleod is seeking a trade-qualified Fitter to join an established industry leader specialising in truck-mounted cranes and mobile lifting solutions.

This is an excellent permanent opportunity for a practical, team-focused tradesperson looking to broaden their skills across mechanical fitting, hydraulics, fabrication, crane assembly and servicing.

While a Mechanical Fitter or Fitter and Turner is preferred, applications are also welcomed from Heavy Vehicle Mechanics, Plant Mechanics and Boilermakers with strong mechanical aptitude and a willingness to learn.

The Opportunity

Working within a close-knit workshop team, you will primarily assist with assembling new truck-mounted cranes, along with maintenance and service work.

Tradespeople generally work collaboratively in small teams, with everyone contributing across the broader manufacturing and assembly process. You won’t be restricted to one discipline—the team is looking for someone open-minded, adaptable and willing to assist wherever needed.

Your responsibilities may include:

  • Mechanical fitting and assembly of new truck-mounted cranes
  • Installing and working with hydraulic components and systems
  • Completing maintenance, servicing and mechanical repairs
  • Assisting with basic welding and fabrication work
  • Diagnosing mechanical and hydraulic faults
  • Working collaboratively with fitters, boilermakers and other trades
  • Maintaining a safe, organised and productive workshop

About You
You will ideally have:
  • A recognised trade qualification as a Mechanical Fitter, Fitter and Turner, Heavy Vehicle Mechanic, Plant Mechanic or Boilermaker
  • Strong mechanical aptitude and practical problem-solving skills
  • An interest in learning hydraulics, welding and other trade disciplines
  • A flexible attitude and willingness to contribute across all areas of the workshop
  • A team-focused approach and strong work ethic
  • A commitment to quality workmanship and safe work practices

What’s on Offer
  • Permanent, stable employment with OT available
  • Competitive rate of $43–$45 per hour, with some flexibility for an exceptional candidate
  • Specialist training in areas such as hydraulics and basic welding
  • Opportunities to become multi-skilled across crane assembly, fitting, fabrication, and servicing
  • Supportive team environment with exceptional employee tenure
  • Stable local, workshop-based work
  • Early finish every Friday
 

If you are an adaptable tradesperson looking for stable local work, excellent training, and the opportunity to expand your technical skills, we would love to hear from you.

Apply now by submitting your current resume.

job.title: Information Release Officer
job.description:
About the Role

We are seeking a highly organised and detail-oriented Information Release Officer to join our clients team. This role is responsible for supporting the implementation and administration of information release processes in accordance with relevant legislation and departmental requirements.
The successful candidate will manage requests for information, undertake detailed records reviews, and ensure compliance with legislative obligations including the Freedom of Information Act 1992 (WA), State Records Act 2000, National Redress Scheme for Institutional Child Sexual Abuse Act 2018, and the Children and Community Services Act 2004.

This position may involve reviewing records that are highly sensitive and confronting in nature and requires a professional, resilient and empathetic approach.

Offered on a temporary basis for a period of up to 12 months.

Key Responsibilities
  • Process and administer requests for the release of information in accordance with relevant legislation and policies.
  • Research, analyse and review records to determine appropriate disclosure requirements.
  • Interpret and apply legislative requirements, regulations and departmental procedures.
  • Assist in the coordination and management of summonses, subpoenas and court orders.
  • Prepare, review and vet records and files for release to courts and other authorised agencies.
  • Provide high-quality advice and support regarding information release processes.
  • Maintain accurate records and documentation to support compliance and audit requirements.
  • Collaborate effectively with internal stakeholders and external agencies to achieve timely outcomes.
  • Undertake a range of information management activities to support client needs and organisational objectives.
About You

To be successful in this role, you will demonstrate:

Essential Requirements
  • Strong analytical, research and problem-solving skills.
  • Excellent interpersonal, negotiation and conflict resolution skills.
  • Proven ability to build effective working relationships with stakeholders at all levels.
  • Well-developed written and verbal communication skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to interpret and apply legislation, policies and regulations.
  • Knowledge and understanding of legislation supporting the release of information, including the Freedom of Information Act 1992 (WA).
  • Ability to work both independently and collaboratively within a team environment.
  • High attention to detail and commitment to confidentiality.
Desirable
  • Experience interpreting and providing advice on Freedom of Information (FOI) legislation in Western Australia.
  • Previous experience in records management, information governance, legal administration, FOI, privacy, or a related compliance environment.
Why Join?
  • Meaningful work that supports transparency, accountability and community outcomes.
  • Opportunity to develop specialist expertise in information access and legislative compliance.
  • Supportive and collaborative team environment.
  • Ongoing professional development opportunities.
If you are a motivated professional with a strong understanding of information management and legislation, and you are seeking a rewarding role where your expertise can make a genuine impact, we encourage you to apply.

job.title: Assistant Director Cultural Safety Learning
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is recruiting a Cultural Safety Learning Lead for a Federal Government Client. This role is a full time labour hire role and can be based our of any Major Capital City. 

This is an exciting opportunity to lead the development and implementation of cultural safety learning initiatives that strengthen workforce capability and improve outcomes for First Nations peoples with disability.

The successful candidate will play a key role in embedding cultural safety across the organisation through learning, capability development, stakeholder engagement, and strategic leadership.

About the Role
As the Cultural Safety Learning Lead, you will drive the design and delivery of learning and development initiatives that build organisational capability and support culturally safe practices across the workforce.

Working closely with First Nations communities, internal stakeholders, and senior executives, you will lead the development of programs that support improved access to services and better outcomes for First Nations peoples.

This is a highly influential role suited to an experienced professional with strong leadership, stakeholder engagement, learning and development, and strategic policy capabilities.

Key Responsibilities
  • Lead the design, development and implementation of cultural safety learning programs and workforce capability initiatives.
  • Provide high-level strategic, policy and cultural safety advice to senior leaders and executive stakeholders.
  • Prepare complex documentation, including ministerial briefs, executive papers, submissions and reports.
  • Lead consultation and co-design activities with First Nations peoples, communities, organisations and key stakeholders.
  • Build and maintain strong relationships across government, community and organisational networks.
  • Represent the agency in meetings, forums, committees and working groups.
  • Collaborate with HR, Learning and Development and operational teams to align capability initiatives with strategic workforce priorities.
  • Monitor program delivery, risks, performance measures and outcomes, providing regular reporting and recommendations.
  • Lead, mentor and support team members while fostering a positive, culturally safe and high-performing work environment.
  • Champion innovative and strengths-based approaches to capability development and organisational change.
About You
You will bring a strong combination of leadership, cultural capability, stakeholder engagement and learning and development expertise.

Essential Skills and Experience
  • Demonstrated experience building genuine partnerships with First Nations peoples, communities and organisations.
  • Experience leading learning and development programs, capability uplift initiatives or workforce development strategies.
  • Strong understanding of cultural safety principles and how they can be embedded across organisations.
  • Exceptional stakeholder engagement, consultation and co-design capabilities.
  • Strong analytical and critical thinking skills with experience providing evidence-based advice.
  • Excellent written communication skills, including preparing executive briefs, reports and strategic documentation.
  • Proven ability to lead teams, manage priorities and deliver outcomes in complex environments.
  • Strong understanding of governance, risk management and program delivery frameworks.
Knowledge and Capability
  • Understanding of First Nations cultures, histories, perspectives and community engagement approaches.
  • Knowledge of cultural safety frameworks and best practice approaches.
  • Understanding of Commonwealth policy development and government decision-making processes.
  • Experience applying strategic planning, governance and performance monitoring principles.
  • Knowledge of project and program management methodologies.
  • Ability to use evidence and data to inform decision-making and continuous improvement.
Highly Desirable
  • Demonstrated experience working with First Nations peoples, communities and/or organisations.
  • Qualifications in Education, Training, Human Resources, Organisational Development or a related field.
  • Experience designing and delivering learning programs within government, community or service delivery settings.
  • Certificate IV in Training and Assessment (TAE40122 or equivalent).
Desirable
  • Experience working within the NDIA, NIAA, Department of Health and Aged Care, Disability sector, or Aboriginal Community Controlled Organisations.
  • Tertiary qualifications in Indigenous Studies, Public Policy, Social Sciences, Law, Education or a related discipline.
Why Apply?
  • Make a meaningful impact on outcomes for First Nations peoples with disability.
  • Lead a nationally significant cultural safety and workforce capability initiative.
  • Work collaboratively with First Nations communities and senior government stakeholders.
  • Join a team committed to inclusion, cultural safety and continuous improvement.
  • Drive positive organisational change and influence workforce capability at a strategic level.
Apply Now If you are passionate about cultural safety, capability development, and creating meaningful change for First Nations peoples and communities, we encourage you to apply.

job.description:
Chandler Macleod is recruiting on behalf of our Federal Government client for an experienced Legislative Policy & Reform Assistant Director to join a high-performing team responsible for leading complex legislative and regulatory reform initiatives within the disability sector.
This is an exciting opportunity for a policy professional with strong Federal Government experience to contribute to significant policy and legislative reforms that support regulatory and safeguarding outcomes across Australia.

About the Role As the Legislative Policy & Reform Assistant Director, you will provide strategic policy, legislative and regulatory advice while leading the development and implementation of reform initiatives. You will work closely with senior executives, government agencies and key stakeholders to shape policy outcomes and drive legislative change.

The successful candidate will lead complex policy projects, prepare high-quality executive materials and contribute to cross-government reform programs in a dynamic and high-profile environment.

Key Responsibilities
  • Lead the development, review and reform of legislation, regulations and policy frameworks.
  • Provide strategic advice on emerging regulatory, safeguarding and operational issues.
  • Prepare high-quality briefs, submissions, executive papers, correspondence and Cabinet-related materials.
  • Develop consultation strategies and coordinate stakeholder engagement activities.
  • Manage complex policy and legislative reform projects.
  • Support cross-agency and intergovernmental reform initiatives.
  • Identify legislative, regulatory and operational risks and develop mitigation strategies.
  • Support the implementation of policy and legislative reforms through governance and change management activities.
  • Build productive relationships with Commonwealth, State and Territory agencies, disability sector stakeholders and internal business areas.
What We're Looking For To be successful in this role, you will demonstrate:
Essential Experience
  • Strong policy development experience within the Australian Federal Government.
  • Experience developing legislative policy and providing legislative or regulatory advice.
  • Proven ability to prepare briefs, submissions, ministerial correspondence and executive materials.
  • Experience engaging and consulting with a broad range of stakeholders.
  • Strong written communication, analytical and project management skills.
Highly Desirable
  • Experience leading or contributing to legislative reform programs.
  • Understanding of regulatory environments and government decision-making processes.
  • Experience supporting policy implementation and change management activities.
Key Deliverables The successful contractor will:
  • Deliver high-quality policy and legislative advice to senior decision-makers.
  • Lead or contribute to legislative and regulatory reform projects.
  • Develop policy positions, drafting instructions and reform implementation strategies.
  • Coordinate stakeholder consultation and engagement activities.
  • Provide governance and executive support through briefing materials and committee papers.
  • Manage project milestones, risks and reporting requirements.

  • Long-term contract through to October 2027.

  • Flexible location arrangements across multiple capital cities.

  • Opportunity to contribute to nationally significant policy and legislative reform initiatives.

job.title: Financial Accountant
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is seeking experienced Financial Accountants for an exciting labour hire opportunity within a Federal Government agency's Financial Statement Team.
This is an excellent opportunity for finance professionals with strong Australian Government financial reporting experience and advanced knowledge of TechnologyOne (TechOne) to contribute during a critical financial statement preparation period.

Working Arrangements
  • Sydney-based role with a fixed office location
  • Required to work five days onsite during the first week
  • Thereafter, a hybrid arrangement of:
    • 2 days in the office
    • 3 days working from home

About the Role: As a Financial Accountant, you will play a key role in supporting the agency's financial reporting obligations, month-end and year-end processes, statutory compliance, and audit activities.
The successful candidate will bring demonstrated experience working within a Federal Government environment and possess a strong understanding of APS financial reporting frameworks and requirements.

Key Responsibilities
  • General ledger management, account reconciliations, and journal processing
  • Month-end and year-end financial close activities
  • Financial reporting and transaction processing using TechnologyOne (TechOne)
  • Preparation and lodgement of Business Activity Statements (BAS)
  • Preparation and reconciliation of Fringe Benefits Tax (FBT) returns
  • Management of monthly and annual actuals and cash management through CBMS
  • Preparation of supporting schedules, audit working papers, and financial statements using PRIMA
  • Supporting internal and external audit requirements
  • Liaising with internal stakeholders, auditors, and the Department of Finance
  • Ensuring compliance with Australian Accounting Standards, the PGPA Act, and Commonwealth financial reporting requirements
Essential Experience To be considered for this opportunity, you will have demonstrated experience in:
  • Commonwealth Government and/or APS financial accounting and reporting
  • TechnologyOne (TechOne), including:
    • Financial reporting
    • Transaction processing
    • Account reconciliations
    • General ledger management
  • Preparation and lodgement of BAS
  • FBT return preparation and reconciliations
  • CBMS, including monthly and annual actuals and cash management
  • Financial statement preparation and audit support using PRIMA
  • Australian Accounting Standards and Commonwealth reporting frameworks
  • Building effective relationships with stakeholders across government

job.title: Senior Procurement Specialist
job.description:
About the company:

The agency is responsible for advancing Australia’s interests internationally and supporting the country’s diplomatic, economic, development, security and international policy objectives.
It works with governments, international organisations, businesses, communities and partners across the region and around the world to strengthen relationships, support Australia’s national interests and respond to emerging global challenges.
The agency delivers a broad range of international programs and initiatives, including work focused on cyber security, critical technology, international development, regional partnerships and cooperation across the Indo-Pacific.
 
About the Team

You will be part of a dynamic team responsible for delivering the SEA-PAC Cyber Program and other related activities.
The team works across cyber cooperation initiatives and partners closely with business areas, finance, procurement and enabling teams to deliver effective program outcomes.
You will report to the Head of the SEA-PAC Cyber Unit and work closely with:
  • Directors across the Pacific and Southeast Asia Cyber Cooperation areas
  • The Assistant Secretary, Cyber Affairs and Critical Technology
  • The Ambassador for Cyber Affairs and Critical Technology
  • Finance, procurement and enabling teams
  • Internal and external program stakeholders
The team operates in a changing environment, so you will need to be comfortable managing competing priorities, working
 
About the Role
As the Procurement Specialist, you will lead procurement activities across a range of cyber and critical technology initiatives.
You will be responsible for the full procurement lifecycle, from developing procurement strategies and engaging the market through to tendering, negotiation, contract execution and ongoing contract management.
You will also provide specialist advice on funding, financial management, risk, probity and procurement governance.
A key part of the role is ensuring procurement activities are structured appropriately across Official Development Assistance (ODA), non-ODA and departmental funding, while meeting government procurement and financial requirements.
You will need to balance compliance with practical outcomes and provide clear advice that helps program teams make sound procurement decisions.
 
Key Responsibilities
 
  • Lead end-to-end procurement activities, from planning and market engagement through to contract execution and closure.
  • Develop procurement strategies, tender documentation and contract arrangements.
  • Provide strategic procurement advice to program teams and senior leaders.
  • Manage contracts, supplier performance, KPIs, SLAs and financial commitments.
  • Ensure procurement activities comply with the Commonwealth Procurement Rules and agency policies.
  • Manage ODA, non-ODA and departmental funding requirements in partnership with finance teams.
  • Oversee procurement systems, purchase orders, invoicing and financial reconciliation.
  • Manage procurement risks, probity requirements and conflicts of interest.
  • Prepare procurement, financial and risk briefs for senior stakeholders.
  • Maintain procurement records, trackers and reporting, and identify opportunities to improve processes and governance.
 
You Must Have
 
  • Strong procurement experience, including managing the full procurement lifecycle from planning through to contract closure.
  • Experience managing both simple and complex procurements.
  • Strong knowledge of the Commonwealth Procurement Rules (CPRs) and government procurement requirements.
  • Experience developing procurement strategies, tender documentation and contract arrangements.
  • Experience managing tenders, evaluations, negotiations and contract execution.
  • Strong contract management skills, including monitoring supplier performance, KPIs, SLAs and financial commitments.

job.title: Legislative Policy & Reform - Assistant Director
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is recruiting on behalf of our Federal Government client for an experienced Legislative Policy & Reform Assistant Director to join a high-performing team responsible for leading complex legislative and regulatory reform initiatives within the disability sector.
This is an exciting opportunity for a policy professional with strong Federal Government experience to contribute to significant policy and legislative reforms that support regulatory and safeguarding outcomes across Australia.

About the Role As the Legislative Policy & Reform Assistant Director, you will provide strategic policy, legislative and regulatory advice while leading the development and implementation of reform initiatives. You will work closely with senior executives, government agencies and key stakeholders to shape policy outcomes and drive legislative change.

The successful candidate will lead complex policy projects, prepare high-quality executive materials and contribute to cross-government reform programs in a dynamic and high-profile environment.

Key Responsibilities
  • Lead the development, review and reform of legislation, regulations and policy frameworks.
  • Provide strategic advice on emerging regulatory, safeguarding and operational issues.
  • Prepare high-quality briefs, submissions, executive papers, correspondence and Cabinet-related materials.
  • Develop consultation strategies and coordinate stakeholder engagement activities.
  • Manage complex policy and legislative reform projects.
  • Support cross-agency and intergovernmental reform initiatives.
  • Identify legislative, regulatory and operational risks and develop mitigation strategies.
  • Support the implementation of policy and legislative reforms through governance and change management activities.
  • Build productive relationships with Commonwealth, State and Territory agencies, disability sector stakeholders and internal business areas.

Essential Experience
  • Strong policy development experience within the Australian Federal Government.
  • Experience developing legislative policy and providing legislative or regulatory advice.
  • Proven ability to prepare briefs, submissions, ministerial correspondence and executive materials.
  • Experience engaging and consulting with a broad range of stakeholders.
  • Strong written communication, analytical and project management skills.
Highly Desirable
  • Experience leading or contributing to legislative reform programs.
  • Understanding of regulatory environments and government decision-making processes.
  • Experience supporting policy implementation and change management activities.

job.title: Grant Executions Officer
job.description:
